page.layout: One column of running text; in the right margin beside the first and fifth lines, two marginal notes "Cap.7."; running head above the text; catchword "cere" at lower right.

main_text.p: bro de Locis affectis quinto, aliena quadā Cap.7.corruptione, qualis ob morsum ferarum contingit sanguinem, quandoq; in bilem mutari,ait. Praeterea lōge [?] aliter corrumpitur ipse sanguis a pestilenti aere, & venena to,quàm transpiratione prohibita, quamuis nostrum corpus, tum esse perspirabile maxime sit necessarium. Propterea Galenus libro de Differentiis febrium primo, Cap.7.humorum putredine, quae fit in uasis duo statuit genera: quorum alterum fit superate natura: alterum vero ipsa superata. At quae sit putredo a vincente natura, non simplex est, quemadmodum ait Galenus, sed aliqd in se continet concoctionis. Nam qui putrescit humor vi concoctrice, quae in uasis manet, ad talem pervenit alterationem. Et haec putrefactio concoctio est, quae semper ad unam puris speciem terminatur, coloremq; ac consistentiam suscipit & odorem. Ob id ex tali humore concoctionem a uase continenti suscipiente urina fit optima, quae album, lene, & aequale, minimeq; foetidum habet sedimentum. Alterum putredinis genus fit, cum ea vis concoquendi adeo imbecillis est facta, ut nullam transmutationem ad optimum possit amplius facere

page.notes: Printed text ends with "fa-" at the line end; the catchword "cere" completes it as "facere". Long s normalised to s; u/v and i/j normalised. Greek "lōge" is a doubtful reading (printed "loge" with an accent over the second vowel, possibly Greek λόγῳ); marked [?]. A large dark ink stain covers the middle of lines 5 to 7 ("tum esse", "Propterea"), and the words there are read with some uncertainty. The paragraph is treated as one continuous paragraph, since no line is indented. Printed "aliqd" is kept as printed with its abbreviation mark.
